draft.title: Waybill Investment Case
draft.purpose: Evaluate Waybill's value proposition and operational viability for investment.

sections.heading: Customer Pain
sections.content: Hardware teams waste 20+ hours/month on procurement (E2). Manual processes involve 5+ distributor emails, 3-carrier tracking, and customs clearance delays. 85% of engineers report stock visibility issues (E5).

sections.heading: Value Creation
sections.content: Waybill automates end-to-end procurement: 10x faster sourcing (E3), 70% lower freight costs (E12), and 98% invoice-matching accuracy (E5). Reduces engineer time spent on procurement from 20h/month to 2h/month.

sections.heading: Monetization vs. Value
sections.content: Revenue model: 15% fee on procurement value (E3). Customer value includes 30% cost savings (E12) and 50% faster time-to-market (E5). Unknown: pricing elasticity for large orders.

sections.heading: Business Model
sections.content: SaaS subscription for 300+ active users (E9). 80% revenue from enterprise hardware firms. 40% CAC ratio (E12). 6-month LTV-to-CAC ratio. Unknown: churn rate for SaaS tiers.

missing_inputs.why: Validate 30% churn hypothesis for SaaS model
Calculate revenue scalability against 15% fee margin
Quantify logistics cost savings vs. competitors

draft.decision_question: Can Waybill achieve 50% CAC payback with 30% churn and 15% fee margins?
draft.next_action: Request E13-E15 to validate scalability assumptions
draft.completion_test: Confirm 20% MoM revenue growth vs. 40% CAC ratio and 30% churn

quantitative_logic.reason: CAC ratio is not a standard metric; LTV-to-CAC ratio requires explicit LTV calculation not provided.

grounding.reason: 85% stock visibility claim lacks source evidence in company_evidence; E5 only mentions inventory matching.

usefulness.reason: Narrow focus on CAC payback ignores broader market validation and customer acquisition risks.

stage_fit.reason: 300+ SaaS users with 80% enterprise revenue is premature for a 3-person S2026 startup.

completion.reason: 20% MoM revenue growth comparison lacks baseline duration for time-based savings calculation.
